headline_findings: Web Bluetooth is Chromium-only (~76% global support, April 2026 per caniuse) and absent from every Safari including iOS/iPadOS, so a band can only talk to goforge.fit on iPhone through a native layer; FitForge's existing zero-dependency SwiftUI WKWebView shell + ForgeBridge (docs/IOS-SHELL-CONTRACT.md) is the correct home for CoreBluetooth with state restoration, not the Capacitor community BLE plugin, which documents bluetooth-central mode but has no state-restoration support (secondary: caniuse, capacitor-community/bluetooth-le README + discussion #679; verified: repo docs).

WHOOP's official support page states the strap stores up to 14 days of unsynced data and catches up over Bluetooth when the phone is near; the prompt's 4-5 day assumption is wrong and the 'on-device logger + sync on connect' pattern should be sized at >=14 days (verified: support.whoop.com).

Android Health Connect's ExerciseSegment carries startTime, endTime, segmentType, repetitions, weight, setIndex and rateOfPerceivedExertion, with per-exercise segment constants such as EXERCISE_SEGMENT_TYPE_BENCH_PRESS = 5 and session type EXERCISE_TYPE_STRENGTH_TRAINING = 70, so set-level strength data has a first-class Android sink; HealthKit only offers workout-level HKWorkoutActivityTypeTraditionalStrengthTraining / FunctionalStrengthTraining and writing needs the companion app plus NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription (verified: androidx source, HKWorkout.h SDK header).

Google Fit APIs (including REST) are supported only until the end of 2026 with no exact shutdown day and signups closed 1 May 2024, so all Android health plumbing must target Health Connect (verified: developers.google.com/fit snippet).

WHOOP's public API v2 (base https://api.prod.whoop.com/developer/v2; cycles, recovery, sleep, workouts, body measurements, webhooks; scopes read:recovery read:sleep read:cycles read:profile read:workout read:body_measurement) is rate-limited to 100 requests/min and 10,000/day per app, which third parties translate to roughly 60-80 connected users at default limits; it is a viable zero-hardware Stage 0 but requires a Cloudflare Worker to hold the OAuth client secret (secondary: third-party docs quoting developer.whoop.com/docs/developing/rate-limiting; verified endpoint shapes from client code).

Aggregators have $300-$400/month floors (Junction/ex-Vital $0.50/user/mo with $300 minimum; Terra Quick Start $399/mo billed annually for 100,000 credits ~500 active auths; ROOK Core $399/mo for 750 active users plus add-ons) so at FitForge's scale direct OAuth integrations with WHOOP, Oura v2, Polar AccessLink v3, Ultrahuman Partner API and Fitbit are cheaper (secondary: Sahha competitor comparison pages, unverified against vendor pages).

Bluetooth SIG's Physical Activity Monitor Service/Profile v1.0 exist as adopted specs but a GitHub code search for 'Physical Activity Monitor' 183E returned 445 hits whose top results are all UUID lookup tables and zero firmware implementations, so the practical GATT stack is Heart Rate 0x180D + Battery 0x180F + Device Information 0x180A + a custom Set-Event service, with Nordic UART (6e400001-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e) for debug streams (verified: bluetooth.com spec pages, Zephyr nus.h; estimate: adoption).

Measured BLE 5 throughput between two nRF52840-DKs at 2M PHY with 251-byte DLE reached 1,373 kbps (Nordic DevZone), i.e. draining 14 days of 1 Hz 2-byte HR samples (~2.4 MB) takes ~14 s at that rate and ~100 s at a conservative 200 kbps phone-side budget (secondary: Nordic DevZone; estimate: derived arithmetic).

Regulatory: the FTC Health Breach Notification Rule amendments (finalized 26 Apr 2024, 89 FR 47028, effective 29 Jul 2024) expressly cover non-HIPAA health apps and connected devices; India's DPDP Rules 2025 were notified 13 Nov 2025 with full compliance due 13 May 2027 (18 months); FDA reissued 'General Wellness: Policy for Low Risk Devices' on 6 Jan 2026 focused on non-invasive physiologic-sensing wearables, keeping HR/HRV/sleep/readiness in wellness while diagnostic claims (SpO2/ECG/AFib/BP for disease) remain device territory (secondary: multiple third-party compliance docs citing the primary sources; official sites egress-blocked).

Pre-certified nRF52840 modules carry their own FCC grants (Raytac MDBT50Q FCC ID SH6MDBT50Q / IC 8017A-MDBT50Q; Nordic 2AEMI-NRF52840) under 47 CFR 15.212 modular approval, leaving the end product with Part 15B SDoC testing (third-party figures ~$1.5-4k per SKU, labs quoting 3-6 weeks and $3-8k per device) while the Bluetooth SIG Declaration ID is the largest single line (third-party notes: Adopter $12,000, Associate $6,000, Innovation Incentive ~$2,500 for <$1M revenue) - the official fee page was blocked, so treat all fee figures as unverified (verified: module FCC IDs from shipping-product compliance docs; secondary: cost figures).

OSS reference stack worth studying: OpenStrap/protocol + edge (WHOOP 4.0/5/MG and Oura decoder, 576 stars, created Mar 2026), bWanShiTong's WHOOP BLE write-up (245 stars), InfiniTime (3,369 stars, C++/FreeRTOS on nRF52832 PineTime), ZSWatch (3,356 stars, Zephyr on nRF5340 via u-blox NORA-B10, $99 WatchDK, MAX32664C heart-rate devkit), Gadgetbridge (codeberg, release 0.92.2 on 11 Jul 2026), Polar BLE SDK (official, Verity Sense/H10/OH1), Bangle.js (nRF52840, Web Bluetooth app loader), Movesense (nRF52832 Whiteboard API, MD/HR+/HR2 variants) - Movesense price, MOQ and country-of-manufacture were NOT found this session (verified: GitHub metadata; not found: Movesense commercials).

FitForge's codebase already has the right primitives: users/{uid} is a whole-bundle document {bundle, updatedAt, schema: 2} reconciled push/pull/ask; workout sessions union-merge by session id; health/cycle/readiness/activeSession prefixes are denylisted from cloud sync; health ingestion is idempotent by (metric, date) and hkUuid - so band set events should land in a new append-only fitforge.band.v1 event log keyed by (deviceId, seq) that is union-merged and promoted into sessions, never written into the LWW bundle directly (verified: apps/web/lib/demo/store.ts, auth/sync.ts, health/store.ts).

detailed_notes:
# Software integration lens - band <-> FitForge

Method note: the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted after the first 10 queries and both allowed WebFetch attempts (developer.whoop.com, bluetooth.com) were egress-blocked. The remainder was gathered from GitHub code/repository search (verbatim source snippets and repo metadata, treated as verified for code facts and as secondary for third-party notes) and from the FitForge repo itself. Everything not found is marked as such.

## 1. Transport paths: what can actually talk to a band

- **Web Bluetooth (navigator.bluetooth)**: ~76% global support (caniuse, Apr 2026) and that is entirely Chromium (Chrome 56+/70+ Windows, Edge 79+, Opera, Samsung Internet). No Safari on any Apple OS; Chrome/Firefox on iOS are WebKit so also no. iOS workarounds are Bluefy (a Web BLE browser app) and the iOSWebBLE Safari extension polyfill - fine for a developer or a demo, not for a product. A PWA has no background BLE: the tab must be foreground, so Web Bluetooth covers only 'phone or laptop on the bench, app open' - which is exactly the strength-training set-logging use case on Android/desktop, and nothing of the 24/7 tracker use case.
- **Capacitor + @capacitor-community/bluetooth-le**: README (verified) requires NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription and bluetooth-central in UIBackgroundModes for background use; discussion #679 (secondary) states the plugin has no CoreBluetooth state restoration, so if iOS suspends the app the connection is not correctly re-established and the app gets only a few seconds per wake. Android 12+ needs runtime BLUETOOTH_SCAN/BLUETOOTH_CONNECT (neverForLocation avoids the location prompt, verified on developer.android.com); background scanning needs a foreground service since Android 10 and OEM Doze variants are hostile (blog-tier).
- **Native companion**: the only path that gives iOS state restoration (Apple doc, verified) and Android foreground-service sync. Crucially, FitForge's iOS shell is already native SwiftUI with zero dependencies and a versioned bridge (ForgeBridge v1), so 'native companion' for iOS means adding a CoreBluetooth engine and band/* messages to the existing shell, not adopting Capacitor. Android has no shell today; Web Bluetooth on Chrome covers Stage 1 foreground logging, and a small native Android app (or Capacitor with a foreground service) is only needed when 24/7 capture matters.

Realistic path: (a) Web Bluetooth for Android Chrome + desktop foreground logging, (b) the existing SwiftUI shell for iOS with restore identifier + bluetooth-central, (c) a native Android companion in Stage 2.

## 2. GATT design and the sync pattern

- Adopt standard services for interoperability: Heart Rate 0x180D (so any HR app, Polar Beat, Zwift etc. can read the band), Battery 0x180F, Device Information 0x180A. Skip FTMS (machines). PAMS/PAMP v1.0 are adopted specs (verified on bluetooth.com) but a GitHub-wide search found only UUID tables and no implementation - adopting it buys nothing today; keep it as an optional future service. Nordic UART (6e400001-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e, verified in Zephyr) is the right debug/stream channel.
- **Custom Set-Event service (proposal, estimate)**: 128-bit vendor base UUID; characteristics: SetEvent (notify): u16 seq, u32 device_ts (s since band epoch, corrected by a phone-set clock as WHOOP does), u16 exercise_id (0 = unknown), u8 reps, u16 concentric_ms, u16 eccentric_ms, u8 confidence (0-100), u8 flags - 15 bytes, so one 244-byte payload after MTU negotiation carries ~16 events; ControlPoint (write): set_clock, sync_from(seq), ack(seq), start/stop session; LogStatus (read): oldest_seq, newest_seq, unsynced_count. Every event is append-only and idempotent by (deviceId, seq).
- **Throughput**: 2M PHY + 251-byte DLE measured 1,373 kbps DK-to-DK (Nordic DevZone, secondary); phones do worse. Even at 200 kbps, 14 days of 1 Hz HR (2.4 MB) drains in ~100 s (own arithmetic). Set events are negligible. Daily aggregates for readiness (the fitforge.health.v1 shape) are ~190 B/day.
- **WHOOP's pattern (verified)**: the strap stores up to 14 days unsynced and 'catches up' when the phone is near. Reverse-engineered protocol (OpenStrap/protocol, bWanShiTong; secondary): standard HRS exposed openly, one custom service, one writable command characteristic, bond + MTU bump + notify subscriptions, RTC unset until the phone sets it. Size the band's log at >=14 days.

## 3. Health-platform plumbing

- **HealthKit**: strength workouts are HKWorkoutActivityTypeTraditionalStrengthTraining / FunctionalStrengthTraining (verified in HKWorkout.h); there is no set/rep schema, so set detail stays in FitForge's log and HealthKit gets the workout envelope + energy. Writing needs NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription and the share permission, only from the native shell (the shell contract currently fences HealthKit writes OUT of v1). Background delivery is hourly-ish and never wakes a force-quit app.
- **Health Connect**: ExerciseSessionRecord (EXERCISE_TYPE_STRENGTH_TRAINING = 70) contains ExerciseSegment with startTime, endTime, segmentType (e.g. EXERCISE_SEGMENT_TYPE_BENCH_PRESS = 5), repetitions, weight, setIndex and rateOfPerceivedExertion - all verified in androidx source. Permissions android.permission.health.READ_EXERCISE / WRITE_EXERCISE (+ distance and active-calories writes for totals). Google Fit APIs end with 2026 (verified), so Health Connect is the only Android target.
- **WHOOP API v2 as Stage 0**: OAuth REST at api.prod.whoop.com/developer/v2 exposing cycles, recovery, sleep, workouts, body measurements, plus webhooks; 100 req/min and 10,000 req/day per app (secondary, multiple independent citations of the official page), roughly 60-80 users at default limits. Recovery carries HRV as RMSSD (milli) not SDNN. A Cloudflare Worker must hold the client secret; that changes FitForge's 'data never leaves your browser' promise for users who opt in.
- **Others (endpoints verified from client code)**: Oura v2 usercollection/{daily_sleep, sleep, daily_readiness, daily_activity, heartrate, workout, daily_stress}; Polar AccessLink v3 users/sleep/{date} and users/nightly-recharge/{date} (HRV avg, HR avg, breathing rate); Garmin Health API wellness-api/rest/{dailies, sleeps, activities, backfill} on a push model (partner approval and cost not found); Fitbit Web API still used by 2026 projects; Ultrahuman Partner API is a simple key-authenticated GET metrics?email=&date=. Strava is export-only (200 req/15 min, 2,000/day).
- **Aggregators (secondary, competitor-authored pages)**: Junction $0.50/user/mo with $300 minimum; Terra $399/mo annual; ROOK $399/mo for 750 users plus add-ons; Spike acquired by Raintree (Jul 2026), prices not found; Thryve not found. At FitForge's scale, three or four direct integrations cost less than one aggregator floor.

## 4. Firmware/app lifecycle, sync design, privacy

- **OTA**: Nordic DFU libraries are the de-facto standard (859/587 stars); Capacitor wrappers exist but have 1-2 stars - vendor Nordic's native libs inside the SwiftUI shell (and a future Android app). During prototyping use nRF Connect / nRF Device Manager apps. Zephyr projects (ZSWatch) use MCUmgr/SMP instead - pick one at Stage 2 based on the SDK.
- **Pairing UX**: bond once (LE Secure Connections), remember by identity address, show a single 'Band' card in Profile mirroring the existing Apple Health card (status, last sync, unsynced count, disconnect keeps data). Multi-device: the band is the source of truth for events; phones are collectors; events carry deviceId + seq so two phones can both collect without duplication.
- **Sync design that fits FitForge**: cloud sync is a whole-bundle LWW document {bundle, updatedAt, schema: 2} with push/pull/ask reconcile; the workout log is { version: 1, sessions: [] } union-merged by session id; health keys are denylisted from the sweep. Therefore band data must be its own store, fitforge.band.v1, an append-only event log keyed by (deviceId, seq) with device_ts and receivedAt, merged by set-union on every import path (never LWW), device-local by default (add the prefix to SYNC_DENYLIST_PREFIXES), included in file export. 'Promotion' turns accepted events into rows inside a normal session via the existing logging path, so the trainer/volume/progression code never learns about the band. Raw IMU never leaves the band; daily HR/HRV/sleep/temp aggregates computed on the phone land in fitforge.health.v1 through the existing idempotent ingestBatch (metric, date), with a new source tag and per-source baselines (HealthKit SDNN vs band RMSSD).
- **Privacy/regulatory**: HIPAA does not apply to a consumer wellness app; the FTC HBNR as amended (effective 29 Jul 2024, 89 FR 47028; secondary) does cover non-HIPAA health apps and connected devices, which is the posture FitForge inherits the moment a Worker holds WHOOP tokens or a band syncs health data. GDPR Art. 9 special-category rules apply to HR/HRV/sleep and derived flags. India's DPDP Rules were notified 13 Nov 2025 with full compliance by 13 May 2027 (secondary). Apple 5.1.3: no third-party advertising/marketing/data-mining use, no false HealthKit writes, no personal health information in iCloud (secondary quote). The repo's existing laws (health never syncs silently, consent gate, deletion path) already encode most of this.

## 5. Regulatory classification of the device

- FDA reissued the General Wellness guidance on 6 Jan 2026 (secondary, several independent citations) focused on non-invasive physiologic-sensing wearables and user notifications: HR, HRV, sleep, skin-temp trend and a 'readiness' verdict stay wellness if claims stay lifestyle-oriented; SpO2/ECG/AFib/BP framed around disease are device claims. Design rule: show SpO2 at most as a wellness trend, never a threshold alert, until counsel reviews the 2026 examples.
- FCC: nRF52840 modules with modular approval (Raytac MDBT50Q FCC ID SH6MDBT50Q verified from two shipping products' compliance docs; Nordic 2AEMI-NRF52840 secondary) let the end product skip 15.247 intentional-radiator testing (third-party estimates: saves ~$5-15k) and owe only Part 15B SDoC (~$1.5-4k per SKU) plus labeling; lab quote tables seen: 3-6 weeks, $3-8k per device (secondary). Grantee code $60.
- Bluetooth SIG: Declaration ID fees per third-party notes are Adopter $12,000, Associate $6,000, with an Innovation Incentive of ~$2,500 for sub-$1M-revenue companies; acceptance normally 1 working day. The official fee page was blocked - verify; the prompt's $9,600 was not corroborated.
- CE-RED (no modular approval; whole device tested), UKCA, BIS CRS in India, UN38.3 + IEC 62133 for the cell, RoHS/REACH, Prop 65: no cost or time figures found this session.

## 6. OSS to study (not depend on)

OpenStrap/protocol + edge (WHOOP 4/5/MG + Oura decoders, 576 stars, 2026); bWanShiTong's WHOOP write-up (245 stars); atria (Swift local-first WHOOP companion, 149 stars) - the best model of 'local-first band companion on iOS'. InfiniTime (3,369 stars, nRF52832, FreeRTOS, no Zephyr) and ZSWatch (3,356 stars, nRF5340 NORA-B10, $99 WatchDK, MAX32664C HR devkit on nRF54L15) - the two firmware architectures to compare. Bangle.js App Loader (571 stars) proves a Web Bluetooth-only toolchain. Gadgetbridge (codeberg, 0.92.2 Jul 2026) is the protocol encyclopedia incl. Xiaomi AuthKey pairing; atc1441's MiBand 9/10 BES2700 work and Band 10 protobuf BLE repos cover the newest Xiaomi bands. Polar BLE SDK is official and covers Verity Sense (PPG + IMU, offline recording) - a strong readiness-data prototype. Movesense: nRF52832 Whiteboard/FreeRTOS, ECG/HR + 9-axis IMU, CR2025, MD/HR+/HR2 variants, MDS libs for iOS/Android/Flutter/RN/.NET; price, MOQ, licence and 'made in Finland' were not verifiable this session (movesense.com blocked) - treat as open.

## 7. Recommended architecture in three stages

**Stage 0 - API step (no hardware, 2-4 focused weeks).** New workers/connect Cloudflare Worker cloned from workers/coach (Firebase ID-token verification, per-uid KV rate limit) holding OAuth secrets for WHOOP, Oura, Polar, Ultrahuman (Garmin if accepted, Fitbit optional); stateless pass-through that normalizes provider JSON into fitforge.health.v1 daily points (sleep min, RHR, HRV with method tag, wrist-temp deviation where available, active kcal) and workout samples; webhooks for WHOOP. Web: apps/web/lib/health/providers/*.ts adapters feeding the existing ingestBatch; Profile 'Connected devices' card next to the Apple Health card; explicit consent copy naming the Worker hop; extend hrvSdnn to hrv{value, method} or add hrvRmssd so baselines never mix. Privacy: encrypted tokens in KV, no health rows stored server-side, HBNR/DPDP notices, retention and delete path wired to the existing erase flow.

**Stage 1 - prototype band (off-the-shelf).** Two devices: Polar Verity Sense (or Movesense HR2 if commercials check out) for 24/7-ish HR/HRV via official SDK on the iOS shell, and Bangle.js 2 (nRF52840, JS, Web Bluetooth loader) for on-wrist rep counting because it can be programmed and driven from Chrome with zero native code. Codebase: apps/web/lib/band/ with a BandTransport interface (connect, subscribe, syncSince(seq)) and two implementations - WebBluetoothTransport (Android Chrome/desktop) and BridgeTransport (new ForgeBridge messages band/scan, band/connect, band/event, band/syncStatus, band/dfu). New store fitforge.band.v1 (append-only events, union merge, denylisted from cloud sync, in file export). Workout player: an 'observed set' chip that pre-fills reps/tempo for the current set with accept/correct, mirroring the check-in's 'from Apple Health' pattern. Shell: CoreBluetooth engine with restore identifier + bluetooth-central, bonded-device persistence in native storage, DFU via Nordic iOS library.

**Stage 2 - custom band.** Firmware on Zephyr/nRF Connect SDK using a modular-approved nRF52840 (or nRF54L15) module; GATT = DIS + BAS + HRS + FitForge Set-Event service + NUS + MCUmgr/Secure DFU; on-band ring-buffer log sized >=14 days of aggregates and set events; on-band rep/exercise classifier emitting SetEvents with confidence. Phone side: Android native companion (foreground service, Health Connect writes of ExerciseSessionRecord + ExerciseSegment with repetitions/weight/setIndex/RPE) and iOS shell writes of HKWorkout (traditionalStrengthTraining) once the shell contract's HealthKit-write fence is lifted; readiness aggregates keep flowing through fitforge.health.v1 with a band source tag. Compliance package: wellness-only claims, FCC 15B SDoC on the module grant, Bluetooth DID, CE-RED full test, BIS CRS check, UN38.3 cell docs, FTC HBNR + DPDP + Apple 5.1.3 posture.
